en.title: Subarrays Matching an Adjacent-Comparison Pattern
en.description:
Given an integer array a and a pattern p of length m. The values of p are 1, 0, and −1, requiring the next element to be greater than, equal to, or less than the previous one, respectively. Count the contiguous subarrays of length exactly m+1 whose adjacent comparisons all match the pattern; overlaps are allowed.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n m (2≤n≤10000, 1≤m<n); the second line contains n integers (−10⁹..10⁹); the third line contains m pattern values.
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: [1,4,4,1] starting at 0 and [3,5,5,3] starting at 4 both go up, stay equal, then go down in order; no other window matches, so there are 2 in total.
hints: Convert the adjacent comparisons into a sequence of −1, 0, 1, match the whole pattern with KMP, and after each successful match fall back via the prefix function to keep overlapping matches.
